## Work in progress
This chapter reports the state of the project in November 2026. The results
come from a **small development set** (six engines) and are a first look,
not a conclusion.
:::

## The question

An aircraft engine is monitored flight after flight. At a given flight *t*,
an engineer asks:

> Based on the information available up to flight *t*, is there evidence of a
> concerning trend? What are the plausible causes, and what check should be
> recommended?

Three situations are possible: **gradual ageing** (normal), **compressor
fouling** (needs an engine inspection) and **sensor drift** (needs a sensor
check, not an engine inspection). The task is to build an **agent**: a
language model that reads the documentation, decides which diagnostic tools to
call, and writes a justified recommendation. It must be able to say
"insufficient information" and must never treat a tool's output as a
definitive diagnosis.

## What I built

```{r}
#| label: phm-setup

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(scales)
library(knitr)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
            theme(plot.title.position = "plot",
                  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                  legend.position = "top"))

phm_dir <- here("data", "safran")
```

**1. A rule-based baseline without an LLM.** Alert when the exhaust-gas
temperature margin (1150 K minus the LPT inlet temperature) stays below a
threshold for *p* consecutive usable flights. The persistence rule avoids
alerting on one noisy flight. The supervisors suggested a threshold of
11.5 K; I swept threshold and persistence over a grid on the development
trajectories, then evaluated the chosen setting once on held-out test
trajectories.

**2. A single tool-using agent** (LangChain + Ollama, temperature 0) with
four tools bound to one engine and **cut at the decision time**, so the model
physically cannot look into the future:

| Tool | What it returns |
|---|---|
| `lire_observations(debut, fin)` | sensor readings and flight conditions, ≤ 30 flights per call |
| `estimer_sante(debut, fin)` | six health indicators estimated by a pretrained inverse MLP |
| `calculer_marge(debut, fin)` | the thermal (EGT) margin per flight |
| `regle_seuil_marge()` | *(optional)* the baseline rule's verdict, as one more piece of evidence |

The agent receives the knowledge base as its system prompt and must answer
with one of five actions: continue monitoring, intensify monitoring, request
an engine inspection, request a sensor check, or request additional data.

**3. A fair evaluation harness.** Every model gets the same tools, documents,
prompt, decision time and step limit. Each run records the recommendation,
the number of tool calls, the duration and the full reasoning trace (JSON
lines). The expected action is derived from the hidden scenario labels by
the **evaluator only**; the agent never sees them.

## The baseline: a trade-off between speed and false alarms

```{r}
#| label: fig-phm-grid
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-cap: "Baseline tuning on the development engines: each point is one (threshold, persistence) setting. Lower-left is better: few false alarms on healthy engines and an early detection of fouling."

grid <- read_csv(file.path(phm_dir, "baseline_grid_dev.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
chosen <- filter(grid, seuil_marge == 11.5, persistance == 3)

grid |>
  filter(fouling_detection >= 0.9) |>
  ggplot(aes(normal_fausse_alerte, fouling_retard_median, colour = factor(persistance))) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = .85) +
  geom_point(data = chosen, shape = 21, size = 6, colour = "#D55E00", stroke = 1.2) +
  annotate("text", x = chosen$normal_fausse_alerte + .03, y = chosen$fouling_retard_median + 6,
           label = "chosen: 11.5 K, 3 flights", hjust = 0, colour = "#D55E00", size = 3.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent()) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = .85) +
  labs(x = "False alarms on healthy engines", y = "Median detection delay\nfor fouling (flights)",
       colour = "Persistence (flights)")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-phm-test
#| tbl-cap: "The baseline on held-out test engines, for three settings."

test <- read_csv(file.path(phm_dir, "baseline_test.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
test |>
  transmute(
    `Threshold (K)` = seuil_marge, `Persistence` = persistance,
    `Fouling detected` = percent(fouling_detection),
    `Median delay (flights)` = fouling_retard_median,
    `False alarms (normal)` = percent(normal_fausse_alerte, accuracy = 1),
    `Alerts on sensor drift` = percent(drift_alerte, accuracy = 1)
  ) |>
  kable()

chosen_test <- filter(test, seuil_marge == 11.5, persistance == 3)
```

Requiring persistence pays off (@fig-phm-grid). On the test engines, the
chosen rule detects every fouling case with
`r percent(chosen_test$normal_fausse_alerte)` false alarms on healthy engines,
against `r percent(test$normal_fausse_alerte[test$persistance == 1], accuracy = 1)`
without persistence (@tbl-phm-test). Its limits are structural: it detects
fouling a median of `r chosen_test$fouling_retard_median` flights after it
starts, and it has **no way to tell sensor drift from real degradation**.
It can only say "inspect the engine" or "keep monitoring". That gap is the
reason to try an agent.

## Agents against the baseline

```{r}
#| label: phm-compare

read_run <- \(f, run) read_csv(file.path(phm_dir, f), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(run = run)

runs <- bind_rows(
  read_run("compare_20261109_022944.csv", "Run 1: four local models"),
  read_run("compare_20261109_034614.csv", "Run 2: qwen3:8b, tool errors returned to the model")
) |>
  mutate(systeme = if_else(str_starts(systeme, "baseline"), "Baseline (no LLM)", systeme),
         note = factor(note, levels = c("correct", "acceptable", "wrong", "no_answer"),
                       labels = c("Correct", "Acceptable", "Wrong", "No answer")))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-phm-compare
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-cap: "Outcomes on the six development engines (2 healthy, 2 fouling, 2 sensor drift) at decision flight 250. 'Acceptable' means 'intensify monitoring' where a specific check was expected."

runs |>
  count(run, systeme, note, .drop = FALSE) |>
  filter(n > 0 | note == "Correct") |>
  ggplot(aes(n, systeme, fill = fct_rev(note))) +
  geom_col(width = .7) +
  facet_grid(run ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", labeller = label_wrap_gen(22)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Correct = "#009E73", Acceptable = "#56B4E9",
                               Wrong = "#D55E00", `No answer` = "grey75"),
                    breaks = c("Correct", "Acceptable", "Wrong", "No answer")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:6) +
  labs(x = "Engines", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-phm-compare
#| tbl-cap: "Summary per system and run."

runs |>
  group_by(Run = run, System = systeme) |>
  summarise(Correct = sum(note == "Correct"), Acceptable = sum(note == "Acceptable"),
            Wrong = sum(note == "Wrong"), `No answer` = sum(note == "No answer"),
            `Tool calls (mean)` = round(mean(nb_appels_outils), 1),
            `Time per case (s)` = round(mean(duree_s)),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  kable()
```

What the first runs show (@fig-phm-compare, @tbl-phm-compare):

- **Plumbing matters first.** In run 1, most models produced no usable answer.
  Reading the traces showed why: models asked for flights *after* the decision
  time, the tool raised an exception, and the run died. Returning tool errors
  to the model as text ("window outside the authorised history, correct the
  arguments") let it recover; in run 2, qwen3:8b answered every case.
- **The agent is cautious where the baseline is blind.** On both sensor-drift
  engines, qwen3:8b recommended *intensify monitoring* (acceptable) where the
  baseline said "all fine". But it also missed both fouling cases, while the
  baseline caught one.
- **Cost.** About 15 tool calls and four to five minutes per case with a
  local model, against an instant rule.

So far, the agent is **not better** than a tuned rule on raw accuracy. The
next question is whether it adds value *on top of* the rule.

## Next steps

- Give the agent the baseline rule as a tool (already implemented, flag
  `--with-baseline-tool`) and measure whether it combines the rule's fouling
  detection with its own caution on drift.
- Add trend and change-point tools, so the model does not have to spot a
  slow drift by reading 30-row tables.
- Evaluate on more engines and several decision times, and score the
  *justification* (evidence cited, alternatives considered), not just the
  final action.
